title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Context (pp. 119-121): the dossier studies moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2 by intrinsic, coordinate-free means. As I read the notation (inferred, not stated on the page): J is the 4-element set of 2-torsion points; V_J(k) = Ker(k^J → k, sum), which is 3-dimensional; t is a point of a projective line or conic with tautological bundle O_t(±1); F_t ⊂ V_J(k) is the line attached to t; t_E is the tangent line (Lie algebra) of E; and the underlined ω is a 2-element torsor isomorphic to μ_4^×(k) = {±i}. On p.119 Grothendieck shows that a basis k : t_E ≃ O_t(1) is equivalent to a nonzero element of V_J(t_E) = t_E ⊗ Ker(t_E^J → t_E). Concretely this is a family (δ_i)_{i∈J} satisfying three conditions: a) Σ δ_i = 0; b) the line it spans in V_J(k) is F_t (a proportionality condition); c) compatibility with the 'épinglage de Legendre', i.e. k^{⊗2} must equal an already-known standard isomorphism. He then writes δ_i = φ_i^ω(δ)·δ, with δ a nonzero tangent vector, scalars φ_i^ω(δ) ∈ k^*, and the homogeneity φ(λδ) = λ^{-1}φ(δ) (85). On this page: (86) condition a) becomes Σ_i φ_i^ω(δ) = 0. (87) Condition b) becomes 'the vector (φ_i^ω(δ))_i lies on the line F_t'. This fixes the vector up to an invertible scalar; condition c) then fixes it up to sign, once the auxiliary choice is also made. This matches the fact that a pinning by a square, k^{⊗2}, determines k only up to ±1, i.e. up to the automorphism −1 of E. (88) gives the intrinsic formula: the vector (φ_i^ω(δ)) equals the image of δ under ǩ, twisted by ω, inside O_t(-1)(ω) ≃ F_t ⊂ V_J(k) ⊂ k^J. Condition c) 's'écrit Dieu sait comment — il faudra y revenir': he explicitly leaves it unworked. Finally he records how the φ's depend on the choice of ω, given the isomorphism α : μ_4^× ≃ ω attached to the sought Legendre pinning. (89) states φ_i^{ω'}(δ) = ℓ̇_ω φ_i^ω(δ), with ℓ̇_ω defined via α, so ℓ̇_ω ∈ {±i}. The page ends at 'Posons', just before new notation. Overall purpose: an explicit coordinate description of the trivialization of the tangent line (the invariant differential) carried by the Legendre normal form y² = x(x−1)(x−λ), recast as a torsor-theoretic 'Legendre pinning'.
errors: (89) is stated for an unspecified ω'. For ω' the other element of the 2-element torsor, the transition factor should be a ratio such as ℓ̇_{ω'}/ℓ̇_ω (here = −1), or the formula should be read as relative to a base point. As written the relation is incomplete or ambiguous.
The direction of α is inconsistent. α : μ_4^× ≃ ω, yet ℓ̇_ω is defined as α(ω); presumably α^{-1}(ω) ∈ μ_4^× is meant.
Condition c) is explicitly left unformulated ('Dieu sait comment'), so the characterization of the φ's is incomplete on this page.

Notation in (88) (ǩ(δ) with the superscript and the O_t(-1) subscript, wedge with ω) is too compressed to verify fully. It looks consistent with p.119's ǩ : ť_E ≃ O_t(-1) → O_t(-1)(ω) ≃ F_t, but δ is said to lie in t_E^*, so the domain of ǩ needs a dual identification.

ideas.what: Identifying a trivialization of the tangent line of E with a nonzero vector in V_J(t_E) = t_E ⊗ (sum-zero hyperplane of k^J), normalized by a line F_t and a square-root condition
ideas.modern_name: Rigidification of the invariant differential via full level-2 structure (Legendre family as universal curve with Γ(2)-structure plus differential)

ideas.what: 'Épinglage de Legendre': a pinning determined up to sign, with an auxiliary μ_4^×-torsor (choice of a primitive 4th root of unity)
ideas.modern_name: Legendre structure / torsor under μ_4 for the level-2 moduli; sign ambiguity coming from the automorphism [−1]

ideas.what: Homogeneity and transition laws (85), (89) for the coordinates φ_i^ω(δ) under rescaling of δ and change of ω
ideas.modern_name: Weight/character bookkeeping for sections of line bundles on a moduli torsor

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly leaves open the explicit form of the Legendre-pinning condition c) in terms of the φ_i^ω(δ). This is a minor computational gap, likely filled on later pages or by known Legendre formulas.
missed.quote: et la condition c) s'écrit Dieu sait comment — il faudra y revenir.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of historical interest. The corresponding facts (the Legendre differential dx/y and its sign ambiguity) are standard in Katz–Mazur-style treatments.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine intermediate computation in Grothendieck's intrinsic reworking of the Legendre normal form and level-2 moduli. The ideas are standard (Igusa, Deligne–Rapoport, Katz–Mazur), and the page is mainly bookkeeping of normalizations, with one condition left undone.
transcription_corrections: 'épi-glyphe [?] de Legendre' should read 'épinglage de Legendre' (Grothendieck's term for a pinning).
'(pour i également choisi)' is likely '(pour ℓ̇ [or ω] également choisi)'. The symbol is dotted and doubly underlined in the image.
'pour [-exp-] tenir l'invariance' is probably 'pour [-exp-] tenir compte de l'invariance' or similar; reading uncertain.
The second 'au choix de ω=ω_j' is better read 'au choix de ω = ω_ℓ̇' or similar. The handwriting reads 'au choix de ω = ω_j? ... au choix des ℓ̇', and the machine transcription duplicates it.
In the final line: '(supposé déterminé) associé à l'épinglage de Legendre cherché'.
In (88) the superscript '∨_4' is probably a correction mark/dual sign on ǩ, with δ̌ inside: '(φ_i^ω(δ)) = ǩ(δ̌)∧ω'. The O_t(−1) is a subscript label under ǩ(δ̌).
